Philippines Engineering & Construction Trade Remains Steady Amid Regional Growth

The Engineering & Construction industry in the Philippines reported stable trade figures for the first quarter of 2024, reflecting ongoing regional infrastructure activity and consistent demand from both public and private sectors.

Data released Tuesday by the Philippine Construction Trade Council (PCTC) showed the country’s total exports of engineering and construction services reached $1.14 billion from January to March, up 2.3% from the same period last year. Imports of construction materials and heavy equipment registered $1.29 billion, marking a 2.1% increase year-on-year.

Industry analysts attribute the moderate growth to sustained investments in transport, energy, and residential projects, as well as incremental government spending under the flagship “Build More, Better” program. "We are seeing a continued pipeline of projects, particularly in transport infrastructure and affordable housing," said Edgardo Lim, senior economist at PCTC. "While the growth rate is not dramatic, the sector is benefitting from strong fundamentals and robust demand in the region."

The sector’s trade surplus narrowed slightly to $150 million, reflecting higher imports of steel, cement, and specialized machinery. Industry participants say this is in line with the rollout of several large-scale projects, including the Metro South Commuter Rail Extension and the Mindanao Power Grid Modernization initiative.

Firms such as Solis Construction Group and Pacifica Engineering Services reported steady order books, with both domestic and overseas contracts underpinning activity. "Our overseas contracts, especially in Southeast Asia, remain a reliable source of revenue," stated Anna Rodriguez, chief operating officer at Solis Construction Group.

The Philippine Association of Engineering Contractors (PAEC) noted that labor availability and supply chain conditions have stabilized compared to previous years, helping keep project timelines on track. "We’re not seeing any major disruptions in material supply or workforce availability at this time," commented PAEC president Mario del Rosario. "This stability is crucial as we execute projects under tight schedules."

Industry observers expect the sector to maintain its current pace through the coming months, citing healthy demand from both public infrastructure and private real estate development. "There are no significant headwinds on the horizon," said Lim. "We anticipate continued steady growth as long as current policies and regional economic conditions persist."

The PCTC projects total construction trade for 2024 will reach approximately $9 billion, provided current trends hold and key projects progress as scheduled.
